question: Which statement best describes Data shape?
options: `JSON.parse()` turns valid JSON text into a JavaScript value. The text must follow JSON syntax exactly. It is like reading a form written in an agreed format. Parsing can throw an error when text is broken, so handle that failure when reading user input or network responses. For example, wrap parsing of editable local text in error handling. In practice, catch a syntax error when a user imports malformed JSON text.

JSON supports strings, numbers, booleans, `null`, arrays, and objects. It does not support functions or `undefined`. It is like a small set of building blocks for describing data. Knowing the supported types helps you avoid trying to send JavaScript behavior through a data format. For example, a server response may be valid JSON but contain a string where the app expects a number. In practice, parse a response body only after checking whether the request succeeded.

JSON strings and property names use double quotes. Values cannot contain comments, trailing commas, or unquoted property names. It is like following a strict form template. A JSON file may be rejected even when it looks close to JavaScript object syntax. For example, undefined object properties may be omitted when text is generated. In practice, check parsed fields because valid syntax can still contain the wrong data.

`JSON.stringify()` turns supported JavaScript data into JSON text. It is useful when saving data or sending it over a network. It is like packing a structured form into a message. Some JavaScript values are omitted or transformed, so do not assume every object survives a round trip unchanged. For example, stringify a small preference object before storing it in localStorage. In practice, stringify a small preferences object before storing it locally.
